definitions: A trust in which the beneficiary has no knowledge of the holdings and no right to intervene in their management.
Complete and unquestioning faith or reliance on someone or something.
examples: The politician placed his assets in a blind trust to avoid conflicts of interest.
She had a blind trust in her financial advisor, which proved to be a mistake.
Establishing a blind trust is a common practice for high-ranking officials.
His blind trust in the system led to his downfall.
The terms of the blind trust were designed to ensure impartiality.
